## R Markdown

```{r}
f <- "data/Redacted-2023Coordinated-CVR.xlsx"

# Read the three header rows (rows 2, 3 and 4); skip = 1 ignores only row 1
hdr <- read_excel(f, skip = 1, n_max = 3, col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text")

# Join: row 4 first, then row 2 (the contest), then row 3 (the choice)
# hdr[1, ] is row 2, hdr[2, ] is row 3, hdr[3, ] is row 4
new_names <- paste(hdr[3, ], hdr[1, ], hdr[2, ], sep = "_")

# Delete the leftover "NA" pieces from empty cells
new_names <- gsub("NA_|_NA", "", new_names)

# Read the real data (row 5 onward) with the new names
cvr <- read_excel(f, skip = 4, col_names = new_names)

# Check the result
names(cvr)
```

```{r}
colnames(cvr)
```

```{r}
cvr <- cvr |>
  clean_names()

colnames(cvr)
```
## 0.- Cleaning, Grouping, and Quick-Index - Isabelle ##

Thanks for all the above, Prof. Hughes!

In this section, I'll rename the columns from their CSV names to more easily-readable titles that reflect the candidate votes. Then, the renamed candidates will be separated into additional data tables for their race. Non-Boulder races that do not track data will be removed from the data table. Last, I'll include a short index of tables, for reference while working.

The data in the CVR document is sourced from the results of the Boulder County, CO Election Ballot, for the November 07, 2023 Coordinated Election.  A copy of the 2023 English Sample ballot can be found here: https://assets.bouldercounty.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/2023-English-Sample-Ballot.pdf 

#Quick-Index

Boulder Elections Data Tables

"Shall the state reduce property taxes for homes and businesses, including expanding property tax relief for seniors, and backfill counties, water districts, fire districts, ambulance and hospital districts, and other local governments and fund school districts by using a portion of the state surplus up to the proposition HH cap as defined in this measure?"

### 1. - Maya

"According to the analysis by Boulder Reporting Lab, approximately 19% of voters cast their ballots for the entire Boulder Elevated slate, exclusively voting for its candidates."

For this finding, we can filter the data for people who voted exclusively for Bob Yates for mayor and for Terri Brncic, Jennifer (Jenny) Robins, Tina Marquis, and Tara Winer for city council. The 19% statistic corrects some people's perception that most voters cast ballots for one slate of candidates.

The entire cvr dataset we're working with has 118,787 observations (aka rows). This will be the denominator for getting the percentage.

From below work: 6,522 obs (aka rows aka people) voted exclusively for the Boulder Elevated slate.

6,522/118,787 = 0.0549 = 5.5 % -> far from 19%. What went wrong?

Denominator too big? Looked into it more. This data is for the whole county, not just Boulder City.

So I found the denominator we want from this webpage https://bouldervotes.org/2023.html : "34,249 city ballots counted."

--> 6,522/34,249 = 0.1904289176 = 19%

ChatGPT Convo: https://chatgpt.com/share/6acf194b-6cc0-83e9-bbbe-7a957b454a5a

* **Analysis summary**: See above explanation. Calculated the desired 19% by dividing the number of people who voted for council members Terri Brncic, Jenny Robins, Tina Marquis, and Tara Winer; and who ranked Bob Yates number one of the four mayoral candidates-- by the number of Boulder City ballots cast.

```{r}
cvr_candidates_sentence_one <- cleaned_cvr |>
  filter(
    bob_yates_first == 1,
    terri_brncic_vote == 1,
    jenny_robins_vote == 1,
    tina_marquis_vote == 1,
    tara_winer_vote == 1) |>
  group_by(cvr_number) |>
  view(cvr_candidates_sentence_one)
```

### 2. - Seann

"And about 29% of voters cast their ballots for the entire Boulder Progressive’s slate of candidates. Because Boulder Progressives only endorsed two city council candidates, this percentage includes ballots where voters supported any of the other candidates, including those endorsed by Boulder Elevated or those who were not endorsed by either of the two committees: Silas Atkins, Waylon Lewis, Aaron Gabriel Neyer, and Jacques Decalo."

* **Analysis summary**: 

I came up with this specific code chunk as it allowed me to filter out specifically the progressive candidates of the 2023 races. Filtering out which voters ranked any of these candidates as #1 allowed me to calculate the percentage of voters who cast their votes for the progressive slate. This includes both progressive mayoral candidates and both progressive council candidates. This code chunk displays the voters that ranked Aaron Brockett or Nicole Speer as #1 in the mayoral election, showcasing who placed a Progressive candidate at the top. This code also shows the voters who cast their ballots for Taishya Adams and Ryan Schuchard for Boulder City Council.

```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here
cleaned_cvr |>
filter(
  aaron_brockett_first == 1, 
  nicole_speer_first == 1,
    taishya_adams_vote== 1,
    ryan_schuchard_vote == 1,
    tara_winer_vote == 1,
    waylon_lewis_vote == 1
  )

# Display results of code below this codeblock
```
```{r} 
(34249/118787)*100
```

### 3. - Isabelle

“All the candidates who were endorsed by Boulder Progressives opposed the Safe Zones 4 Kids ballot measure. *Even so, about 26% of voters who backed the Boulder Progressives’ slate of candidates also supported the Safe Zones 4 Kids ballot measure. By comparison, about 88% of voters who only supported the Boulder Elevated slate of candidates also voted for the Safe Zones 4 Kids measure.* All the Boulder Elevated-endorsed candidates backed the measure.”

*Steps:* 
  -Filter for Boulder Progressive ONLY voters. Export dataset.
  -Filter for Boulder Elevated Slate ONLY voters. Export dataset. 
  -Count and determine percentages of SafeZones voters in the two groups.
  
*Boulder Elevated*:  
Bob Yates for mayor 
Terri Brncic, Tina Marquis, Tara Winer and Jennifer Robins for city council. 

*Boulder Progressives*
 Aaron Brockett and Nicole Speer for mayor
 *shouldn't it be /or/?*
 Ryan Schuchard and Taishya Adams for council
-----

*A* 
1.  25.7% of Slate Boulder Progressives said yes to SafeZones. 72.2% of Slate Boulder Progressives said no to SafeZones.
2. 88.0% of Slate Boulder Elevate said yes to SafeZones. 10.8% of Slate Boulder Elevated said no to SafeZones
```{r}
boulder_progressives <- cleaned_cvr |>
filter(aaron_brockett_first == 1 | nicole_speer_first == 1,
       #since only one candidate can be first at a time, legally, we'd want an "OR" here#
       taishya_adams_vote == 1, 
       ryan_schuchard_vote == 1)


nrow(boulder_progressives)
#total = 9839#
```
```{r} 
boulder_progressives |>
  group_by(safezones_yes)|>
  summarise(
    total_yes = sum(safezones_yes),
    total_no = sum(safezones_no))
 
boulder_progressives
#7107 progressives say no#
#2526 progressives say yes#
#9839 progressives in total#

```
```{r}
boulder_elevated <- cleaned_cvr |>
filter( bob_yates_first == 1,
       terri_brncic_vote== 1, 
       tina_marquis_vote == 1, 
       tara_winer_vote == 1,
       jenny_robins_vote == 1)

nrow(boulder_elevated)

#total = 6522#
```
```{r} 
boulder_elevated |>
  group_by(safezones_yes)|>

    total_yes = sum(safezones_yes),
```

*Steps:*

  -Note amount; Divide by total, multiply by 100 to get percent

```{r}

    taishya_adams_vote== 1,

    waylon_lewis_vote == 1,)
```

